topic: Ships - how an icebreaker breaks ice
question: HOW DOES AN ICEBREAKER
BREAK THE ICE?
options: A sharp steel edge cuts through it
Its hull heats the ice and melts it
It crushes it with its own weight
answer_full: It crushes it with its own weight
recap: An icebreaker pushes through sea ice more than two meters thick, without any blade or saw.
explain: The bow of an icebreaker is rounded and slopes gently backwards. So instead of cutting the ice, the ship slides up on top of it.
Then the enormous weight of the ship presses down, and the ice sheet breaks underneath it.
The smooth hull pushes the broken pieces aside, and leaves an open channel for other ships to follow.
